# Claims

1. A method of signaling from a helmet, the method comprising:
   receiving, by a controller of the helmet, a first signal from a first switch mounted on a handlebar of a vehicle;
   in response to receiving the first signal, activating a first light mounted on a rear portion of the helmet;
   receiving, by the controller, a second signal from a second switch mounted on the handlebar; and
   in response to receiving the second signal, activating a second light mounted on the rear portion of the helmet.

2. The method of claim 1, wherein the first signal and the second signal are received over a wireless link between the handlebar and the helmet.

3. The method of claim 2, wherein the wireless link comprises a short-range radio link.

4. The method of claim 1, further comprising deactivating the first light after a predetermined period following activation of the first light.

5. The method of claim 4, wherein the predetermined period is between 5 seconds and 30 seconds.

6. The method of claim 1, further comprising:
   detecting, by an accelerometer of the helmet, a deceleration of the helmet; and
   in response to detecting the deceleration, activating the first light and the second light simultaneously.

7. The method of claim 6, wherein the deceleration exceeds a threshold stored in a memory of the controller.

8. A system comprising:
   a helmet;
   a first light and a second light mounted on a rear portion of the helmet;
   a first switch and a second switch configured to be mounted on a handlebar of a vehicle; and
   a controller configured to activate the first light in response to a first signal from the first switch and to activate the second light in response to a second signal from the second switch.

9. The system of claim 8, wherein the controller is disposed within the helmet.

10. The system of claim 8, further comprising a wireless transmitter coupled to the first switch and the second switch, and a wireless receiver coupled to the controller.

11. The system of claim 10, wherein the wireless transmitter and the wireless receiver communicate over a short-range radio link.

12. The system of claim 8, wherein each of the first light and the second light comprises a light-emitting diode.

13. The system of claim 8, further comprising an accelerometer disposed in the helmet, wherein the controller is further configured to activate the first light and the second light in response to a deceleration detected by the accelerometer.

14. The system of claim 13, wherein the controller is configured to activate the first light and the second light when the deceleration exceeds a threshold.

15. A non-transitory computer-readable medium storing instructions that, when executed by a processor of a helmet, cause the processor to perform operations comprising:
   receiving a first signal from a first switch mounted on a handlebar of a vehicle;
   activating, in response to the first signal, a first light mounted on a rear portion of the helmet;
   receiving a second signal from a second switch mounted on the handlebar; and
   activating, in response to the second signal, a second light mounted on the rear portion of the helmet.

16. The non-transitory computer-readable medium of claim 15, wherein the operations further comprise deactivating the first light after a predetermined period.

17. The non-transitory computer-readable medium of claim 15, wherein the first signal and the second signal are received over a wireless link.

18. The non-transitory computer-readable medium of claim 15, wherein the operations further comprise activating the first light and the second light simultaneously in response to a deceleration of the helmet detected by an accelerometer.
